$comment: The feature matrix of fusedwasi: modules, their features, and a status for each twin (c, python). true = every function of the feature is there and the documents name no limit; false = not there; ["partial", note] = the documents name a limit, and the note names the file that says it. Checked against both twins by tools/check_features.py. See docs/features.md.

wasi:cli.title: Arguments, environment, exit, standard streams, terminals

wasi:clocks.title: Wall clock, monotonic clock, time zone

timezone.note: unstable (feature clocks-timezone) and without a function in both twins: src/fusedwasi/signatures/wasi_p2.json has no c_name and no python_name for them; docs/host_scope.md, 'The size, in numbers', leaves the unstable items out of the 200

wasi:filesystem.title: Files and directories (descriptors, directory streams) and the preopened directories

wasi:http.title: Outgoing http requests; the server side is given by the embedder (unstable in the alpha)

c: bodies are read whole, at most 256 MiB, and http-error-code is always none: docs/host_scope.md, Known limits ('Bodies of http: the C twin reads the answer and sends the request whole')
python: a request is sent whole unless the answer is asked for before its body is finished (then it goes out as the body is written); the answer is read as it comes and the total is at most 256 MiB: docs/host_scope.md, Known limits ('Bodies of http: the C twin reads the answer and sends the request whole'); docs/specs/S0013.md

informationalOutboundResponses.note: unstable, not done: docs/host_scope.md, the paragraph on http ('Not done: send-informational')

c: HTTP/1.1 with one connection for each request, no redirects, no proxies: docs/host_scope.md, Known limits
python: HTTP/1.1 with one connection for each request, no redirects, no proxies: docs/host_scope.md, Known limits

c: https is an internal-error unless the embedder sets state->tls or state->http_send; the library has no TLS code: docs/host_scope.md, Known limits ('https in C needs a TLS hook or http_send'); docs/specs/S0001.md; docs/tls_hook.md

note.python: TLS is built in (ssl.create_default_context(), the system store): docs/host_scope.md, Known limits; see tlsHook for what cannot be set

c: wasi:http/incoming-handler is an export, the embedder makes the request and the outparam; the names are unstable: docs/public_api.md, 'The transport and the server side of wasi:http (unstable in the alpha)'
python: wasi:http/incoming-handler is an export, the embedder makes the request and the outparam; the names are unstable: docs/public_api.md, 'The transport and the server side of wasi:http (unstable in the alpha)'

the answer is read as it comes, and a request goes out as its body is written when the answer is asked for first: docs/host_scope.md, Known limits ('Bodies of http: the C twin reads the answer and sends the request whole'); docs/specs/S0013.md

note.c: deliberate for now: the C twin reads the answer whole, and an answer that breaks after its head fails at `get`: docs/host_scope.md, Known limits ('Bodies of http: the C twin reads the answer and sends the request whole'); docs/specs/S0013.md

http2.note: HTTP/1.1 only: docs/host_scope.md, Known limits ('No HTTP/2, no redirects, no proxies'); tests/test_known_limits.py

redirects.note: a 3xx answer is the answer, no second request: docs/host_scope.md, Known limits; tests/test_known_limits.py

proxies.note: HTTP_PROXY and the like are not read: docs/host_scope.md, Known limits; tests/test_known_limits.py

note.c: state->tls, four functions over any TLS library; the reference hook over Mbed TLS is in tests/tls_mbedtls/: docs/specs/S0001.md; docs/tls_hook.md
note.python: deliberate: TLS is ssl with the system store, no setting and no hook; http_send replaces the whole transport: docs/host_scope.md, Known limits ('The Python twin has TLS and no way to set it'); docs/specs/S0001.md

wasi:io.title: Errors, polling, input and output streams

random.note: C on Windows is BCryptGenRandom, exercised by the scenario default_source in the CI on Windows, not run by hand: docs/host_scope.md, Known limits ('BCryptGenRandom on Windows'); docs/release_checklist.md, section 3

wasi:sockets.title: TCP and UDP sockets, name lookup (unstable in the alpha)

tcpCreateSocket.note: a socket of the family IPv6 is made by the system: where there is no IPv6 the answer is `not-supported`, which is the answer that the WIT gives for it and not a gap of the library; the address checks are tested in both: docs/host_scope.md, Known limits ('IPv6 sockets')

tcp.note: IPv6 sessions are tested in both (scenario ipv6 of tests/test_wasi_p2_sockets.py, skipped without an IPv6 loopback); the options of a listener are given to the accepted socket: docs/host_scope.md, Known limits

udpCreateSocket.note: a socket of the family IPv6 is made by the system: where there is no IPv6 the answer is `not-supported`, which is the answer that the WIT gives for it and not a gap of the library; the address checks are tested in both: docs/host_scope.md, Known limits ('IPv6 sockets')

udp.note: IPv6 sessions are tested in both (scenario ipv6 of tests/test_wasi_p2_sockets.py, skipped without an IPv6 loopback): docs/host_scope.md, Known limits

ipv6.note: the address records are whole, the checks of the addresses are run in both on any machine, and a whole session over ::1 (TCP and UDP) is compared between the twins where there is IPv6 (the test skips without it): docs/host_scope.md, Known limits ('IPv6 sockets'); docs/release_checklist.md, section 3

acceptedSocketProperties.note: fixed 2026-11-05: accept sets on the new socket what the guest set on the listener: docs/host_scope.md, Known limits; docs/release_checklist.md, section 3

wasi_snapshot_preview1.title: WASI 0.1, the snapshot (46 calls), over WASI 0.2

c: the four calls exist and answer NOTSOCK for a descriptor that exists and BADF for one that does not: docs/host_scope.md, Known limits ('An import with no function')
python: the four calls exist and answer NOTSOCK for a descriptor that exists and BADF for one that does not: docs/host_scope.md, Known limits ('An import with no function')

wasi_unstable.title: WASI 0.1, the first snapshot (preview0): 40 calls shared with the snapshot and 5 of its own

ownCalls.note: fd_fdstat_get, fd_filestat_get, fd_seek, path_filestat_get and poll_oneoff differ from the snapshot (the list is `unstable.differs` of src/fusedwasi/signatures/wasi_p1.json)

c: the calls exist and answer NOTSOCK for a descriptor that exists and BADF for one that does not: docs/host_scope.md, Known limits ('An import with no function')
python: the calls exist and answer NOTSOCK for a descriptor that exists and BADF for one that does not: docs/host_scope.md, Known limits ('An import with no function')

host.title: The state and the guest, one for both families (a piece of the library, no imports)

stateAndGuest.note: one State and one Guest serve 0.1 and 0.2: docs/design_model.md, section 12

closedState.note: a closed state stays closed: docs/design_model.md, section 13

memoryBinding.note: C binds pointers, Python takes bytearrays or objects with read and write: docs/design_model.md, section 13

socketPolicy.note: nothing is allowed unless the host says so: docs/host_scope.md, the paragraph on sockets

httpPolicy.note: an outgoing request is refused unless the host allows it: docs/host_scope.md, the paragraph on http

p1OverP2.title: The layer that puts WASI 0.1 over WASI 0.2 (descriptors of 0.1 are resources of the table of 0.2)

openDescriptors.note: the descriptors are made at the first call or by open_descriptors: docs/host_scope.md, 'Changes of 0.1 that 0.2 forced'

unstableCalls.note: the calls of wasi_unstable that differ: docs/public_api.md, the group of 0.1

The Python twin is run on CPython and on.not a feature: which interpreters the CI runs is a property of the CI and of the Python twin as a whole, not of one import (docs/specs/S0009.md, S0010.md, S0011.md)

The C twin on Android is not tested in t.not a feature: where the C twin is run is a property of the CI, not of one import (docs/specs/S0010.md, section 7)

A hard link is what the system lets it b.not a feature: a difference of the systems under the filesystem (Android SELinux, PyPy, Pyodide) that both twins answer with the error code that stands for the error of the system (a Python with no `os.link` answers `unsupported`); the feature `wasi:filesystem/types` is the one that has link-at (docs/specs/S0009.md)

An import with no function: not the libr.not a feature: the library has a function for every import it knows, in both twins (tests/test_known_limits.py, test_the_c_and_the_python_have_a_function_for_the_same_imports; the checker's own list of unlisted functions); what an import that it does not know answers is the choice of whoever links the imports: docs/host_scope.md, Known limits
